transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my body just feels tense all the time now. My neck and shoulders are tight, and even my jaw feels clenched a lot. It’s like I’m bracing for something bad, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or watching TV at night.
Are you experiencing any pain in these tense areas?
Yes, it’s more of an ache from being tight. My neck and shoulders get sore, and my jaw feels clenched a lot. It’s there most of the time, even when I’m just at my desk or trying to watch TV.
Are you having trouble sleeping because of the tension and pain?
I’m not really sure it’s because of the tension or pain. I haven’t paid close attention to that connection. I just know the tightness is there a lot.
Is this tension and pain interfering with your ability to do your job or daily activities?

Yes, it has. I’ve been falling behind on lesson prep and grading, which isn’t like me. And outside of work, I’ve had to give up some of the community-theater stuff I usually help manage because I just couldn’t keep up with all of it anymore.
Have you been feeling anxious or overwhelmed lately?

Yes. I’ve been feeling pretty overwhelmed. My mind keeps jumping around—from whether the contractors missed something with the house, to whether my lesson plans are slipping, whether the robotics kids are falling behind, and then whether I’m disappointing my wife and family because I’m not keeping everything under control. It’s a lot.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?
I don’t know that I’d call it sad, exactly. More worn down and frustrated, maybe. I haven’t really noticed feeling down in that way.
Have you been feeling unusually fatigued lately?

Yes. By the time the last bell rings, I feel completely wrung out. And it’s not the kind of tired where a decent night’s sleep or a quiet Sunday really fixes it. Even something simple like grading a short stack of quizzes feels like I’m pushing through mud.
Have you been withdrawing from social interactions or activities with friends and family because of how you've been feeling?

Yes, somewhat. I haven’t completely stopped seeing people, but I’ve pulled back from things I usually handle. I’m falling behind on lesson prep and grading, and I had to give up parts of the community-theater work I normally manage because I just couldn’t keep up with all of it anymore.
Do you find it hard to stop worrying about things once you start?

Yes. I can tell myself to stop and just focus on the class in front of me, but it doesn’t really work. One small thing, like a late invoice or a student falling behind, starts this whole chain of what-ifs, and I have a hard time shutting it off.
Do you worry about things even when there's no apparent reason to worry?

Yes. Even when there isn’t one clear thing wrong, my mind keeps looking for something. I’ll start wondering if the contractors missed something on the house, then it jumps to whether my lesson plans are falling behind, or if the robotics kids aren’t where they should be. Then I’m worrying that I’m letting my wife or my family down because I’m not keeping everything under control.
Are you experiencing any gastrointestinal problems, such as stomachaches or irritable bowel syndrome?
Not really that I’ve noticed. I mean, I might get a little uneasy in my stomach sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m having stomachaches or anything like irritable bowel problems.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to ignore them?

Yes, that happens. I’ll try to ignore it and get on with teaching, but the same worry keeps circling back. It might start with something small, like an invoice being late or a student slipping behind, and then it turns into one what-if after another. I have a hard time shutting it down.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors to reduce your anxiety?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I might check on things or try to make sure I didn’t miss something, but I wouldn’t call it a ritual or something I have to do in a certain way. It’s more just worrying than doing a specific behavior to make it stop.
Are your worries usually about everyday things like work, finances, or relationships, or are they about more specific fears or concerns?

Mostly everyday things, I’d say. My mind jumps around from one practical worry to the next — like whether the contractors missed something on the house, or whether my lesson plans are slipping, or if the robotics kids are falling behind. Then it turns into worrying I’m letting my wife or family down because I’m not keeping everything under control.
Do you think your worries are worse than what most people would worry about in the same situations?

Yes, I think they probably are. I know everyone worries about work or money or family, but mine seems to jump from one thing to the next and get bigger than it needs to. I’ll be thinking about whether the contractors missed something on the house, then suddenly it’s my lesson plans, then the robotics students falling behind, and then I’m worrying I’m disappointing my wife and family because I’m not keeping everything under control. It feels like more than what other people would do with the same problems.
Do you have thoughts that are intrusive, meaning they come into your mind unwanted and are difficult to dismiss?

Yes, I think so. Not like strange thoughts, exactly, but unwanted worries that pop in and are hard to shake. I’ll tell myself to stop and focus on the class in front of me, but then one small thing—like a late invoice or a student falling behind—sets off a whole chain of what-ifs, and I can’t really shut it down.
Are your worries affecting your relationships with family and friends?

Yes, it has. I don’t think I’m as present with people as I used to be. I’ve started falling behind on lesson prep and grading, and I had to give up some of the community-theater work I usually help manage because I just couldn’t keep up with all of it anymore. It makes me feel like I’m letting people down.
Are there any times or situations when you are able to completely stop worrying about these everyday things?

Not really, no. I can try to tell myself, “Just stop and focus on the class,” and sometimes I manage for a little while, but it doesn’t feel completely gone. One small thing, like remembering an invoice might be late or thinking a student is falling behind, and then it starts this whole chain of what-ifs that I can’t seem to shut down.
Do you have thoughts that are persistent and intrusive, and that you try to suppress or ignore?

Yes. I try to push them away, especially when I’m teaching and need to focus, but it doesn’t really work. One little thing comes up—like a late invoice or worrying about a student falling behind—and then my mind runs through all these what-ifs, and I can’t seem to shut it off.
